text:
sam_h: thinking out loud — can we add a short, signed "region-assert" header at the edge to make proxy routing and compliance decisions cheaper? e.g. clients or edge gateway assert the tenant's region intent so origin can skip cross-region KV reads when allowed.

jin_lee: hmm, would that be authoritative or advisory? how do we prevent spoofing? :thinking_face:

maria_g: if it's signed by our edge cert and has a TTL it could be authoritative for routing decisions. key question: who signs (edge vs client SDK) and who validates?

raul_ops: +1 for edge-signed. if the header is from client SDK that puts burden on customers, and we can't trust arbitrary clients. edge -> sign -> origin validate seems clean.

nina_sec: security concerns: replay, header injection, and fault domains. Need nonces/timestamps and HMAC with short TTL. Also audit trail in logs.

sam_h: proposed header format (very rough):

```
X-Region-Assert: region=eu-west-1; tenant=acct-1234; ts=1710000000; sig=abcdef1234
```

signature = HMAC(edge_key, "region|tenant|ts"). origin validates with edge public key or shared secret.

product-k: what about consent/legal? we still need to record that tenant opted into being served from eu-west. header shouldn't override residency policy, only short-circuit routing where policy allows.

maria_g: agree. header is an optimization and signal for routing; enforcement still done against tenant residency config in control plane. if control-plane mismatch, origin should return 409 or route to policy-check flow.

jin_lee: operationally we need metrics: count of requests routed using header vs control-flow, failures due to expired sigs, mismatch counts. Also trace tag `region.asserted` for debugging.

raul_ops: rollout plan idea: start with readonly paths (embeddings/queries) where data residency is looser, run in permissive mode that logs but doesn't enforce, then flip to enforce for eligible tenants.

nina_sec: permssive mode must still redact PII in logs and avoid logging the full sig. Log only region+tenant+validation-result.

sam_h: fallbacks — if header missing or invalid, fall back to existing lookup flow. But we should avoid extra roundtrips: origin should consult local cache of tenant policy and only call control plane on cache miss.

maria_g: cache invalidation question: if tenant changes residency, how quickly do we honor change? probably respect TTL on cache and provide explicit invalidation via control-plane push. document SLO: stale routing window <= 60s for critical changes?

jin_lee: also consider canary and rollout interactions. During canary we may want edge to assert a canary-region tag so traffic can be steered. header should support optional flags: `hint=canary-42`.

raul_ops: infra-bot: deploy check — "infra-bot: edge cert rotation due in 7 days".

nina_sec: key management: rotate edge signing keys via KMS and distribute to origins for validation via signed JWKS or short-lived secrets. Need automated rollover and grace windows.

product-k: UX: expose a tenant-level toggle "allow-edge-assertions" in console + audit event when toggled. default off for new tenants until we finish legal signoff.

sam_h: open questions I want feedback on: 1) header name/format, 2) signing approach (HMAC vs JWT), 3) TTL and replay window, 4) metrics & alerts, 5) rollout plan and legal guardrails.

maria_g: my take: prefer compact HMAC header (lower CPU) signed by edge with JWKS published for origins, TTL = 30s, permissive=true rollout for 2 weeks, then optional enforce. document in RFC follow-up.

jin_lee: disagree on TTL being that short for high-latency clients; maybe 60s. also ensure monotonic ts or nonce to prevent replay across regions.

nina_sec: accept 60s if we have nonce + per-tenant rate checks. add detection alert for anomaly spikes of validation failures.

raul_ops: I'll add an ops runbook stub: how to diagnose invalid asserts, how to force-remove edge asserts for a tenant, and rollback steps.

sam_h: thanks all — I'll draft a short RFC and include example header, JWKS rotation flow, and rollout checklist. tagging @jin_lee @maria_g for review when ready. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: created RFC draft at https://rfd.redwood.internal/rfcs/region-assert-5170000000 (draft).

product-k: ping if you want legal to look early, I can loop them in.

sam_h: will do. finishing note: want to avoid coupling this header to authentication; keep it separate from user auth tokens so proxies can assert region even for anonymous requests.

maria_g: good call. keeps scope limited.

jin_lee: cool — drop RFC link here when ready and we'll schedule a 30m sync.

sam_h: will post RFC and tentative timeline tomorrow.
